title: The Ferry
author: Alexandre Dias
contentWarnings: Themes of dying peacefully and reunion
excerpt: The ferry left from a small quay she had not, in the specific small careful way, known was there. Aiko had, at sixty-eight, been on a small holiday on a small island off the coast of Kyushu. She had, on the fifth evening, come upon a set of stone steps she had not, in the specific small careful way, seen before. At the bottom was a small wooden ferry. An old man on its open deck. He had, on seeing her, said only: you are the last.

chapters.title: The Quay
chapters.body:

chapters.title: What She Had Brought
chapters.body:
The small careful crossing had, in the specific small careful way, taken some small careful time.

Aiko had, on the small careful open deck, watched the small careful pale gray sky slowly darken into the small careful evening. She had watched the small careful stars come out — one small careful star, then a small careful few, then, in the specific small careful way, a whole small careful sky of small careful stars.

She had, in the specific small careful way, thought about her small careful husband.

She had thought about the small careful first evening they had met, at a small careful university dance in Kyoto in nineteen-seventy-eight, when she had been twenty-one and he had been twenty-three. She had thought about the small careful specific small careful moment at which she had, in the specific small careful way, first known she would, in the specific small careful way, marry him. She had thought about the small careful wedding. She had thought about the small careful house they had, in the specific small careful way, bought together in Fukuoka in nineteen-eighty-two.
